author: Matt Jaworowski
title: Grand Rapids man charged in counterfeit currency scheme - NewsBreak
text:
By Matt Jaworowski ,
14 hours ago
GRAND RAPIDS, Mich. (WOOD) — Michigan State Police say a Grand Rapids man has been arrested in connection to a counterfeit currency scheme.
A Grand Rapids man has been arrested and charged for manufacturing counterfeit $10 bills. (Courtesy Michigan State Police) MSP says the investigation started last October when counterfeit $10 bills were passed at a Dollar General in Benzie County. Investigators eventually determined that identical incidents happened at two stores in Grand Traverse County the day earlier.
Sign up for the News 8 weekly recap newsletter “Over the next five months, troopers coordinated with numerous local, state, federal and out-of-state law enforcement agencies,” MSP said in a statement . “Through extensive investigative efforts, including the execution of multiple search warrants, a suspect was identified.”
That suspect was identified as 56-year-old Matthew Wilson from Grand Rapids.
The Benzie County Prosecutor’s Office approved a warrant in early March for five counts of uttering and publishing counterfeit bills . Wilson was arrested on the warrant on March 27 at a hotel near the Gerald R. Ford International Airport along with two people from Malaysia who had recently traveled to the U.S.
“Following the arrest, troopers conducted additional investigative work and executed a search warrant at the hotel room,” MSP stated. “During the search, troopers recovered additional counterfeit currency, a fraudulent check, multiple electronic devices, and a printer along with materials consistent with the production of counterfeit bills.”
Investigators say they believe Wilson manufactured approximately $30,000 in West Michigan and is alleged to have committed similar offenses in 14 other states. MSP is working with other law enforcement agencies to support their investigations and potentially bring about more charges, including in Iowa and North Dakota.
Wilson has been extradited to Benzie County and was arraigned on Monday on the five felony charges. Each count of uttering and publishing counterfeit bills carries a penalty up to five years in prison and a fine of $2,500.
His bond was set at $250,000. His next court appearance is scheduled for April 20.
